verses.text: “Hey! Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
Why do you spend money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which doesn’t satisfy? Listen diligently to me, and eat that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in richness.
Turn your ear, and come to me. Hear, and your soul will live: and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.
Behold, I have given him for a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander to the peoples.
Behold, you shall call a nation that you don’t know; and a nation that didn’t know you shall run to you, because of Yahweh your God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he has glorified you.”
Seek Yahweh while he may be found. Call on him while he is near.
Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to Yahweh, and he will have mercy on him; and to our God, for he will freely pardon.
“For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways,” says Yahweh.
“For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and doesn’t return there, but waters the earth, and makes it grow and bud, and gives seed to the sower and bread to the eater;
so is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please, and it will prosper in the thing I sent it to do.
For you shall go out with joy, and be led out with peace. The mountains and the hills will break out before you into singing; and all the trees of the fields will clap their hands.
Instead of the thorn the cypress tree will come up; and instead of the brier the myrtle tree will come up: and it will make a name for Yahweh, for an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.”

footnotes.content: The cry "Hey!" stops me—urgent as a merchant calling in the street. Come, everyone, without coin or payment. It's a picture the eye can almost see: water, wine, milk offered freely to the hungry and poor. He means us. The gift is always offered before we think to ask.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I notice how gently this reproof comes—not anger, just a question that turns me around. Why do we chase what fills the belly but starves the soul? He calls us to listen and eat what truly satisfies. The invitation has teeth: know what you're really hungry for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David's mercies are promised everlasting—a covenant older than any we'll make, sure and unfailing. When He says "your soul will live," He means it: life flows from turning the ear toward Him. One breath toward His voice changes everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A witness stands and tells what he has seen. A leader and commander shape what comes next. This verse speaks of the One given for both—the Messiah, our true King. He doesn't rule by force but by the weight of His faithful presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nations you've never met will run to you—not for your power, but because He has glorified you. His glory spills over onto His people like light through an open door. We are vessels, not the source; we carry what He pours in.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "While he may be found"—a reminder that seeking is seasonal, urgent. He does not hide, but there are seasons of drawing near and seasons we miss Him. The time to call is now, while the door stands open and He is listening close.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forsake the way—the whole bent of it. Return, and He meets you with mercy before you finish turning. His pardon is not grudging but freely given, a gift He delights to offer. Repentance is simply coming home to a Father who was always watching the road.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His thoughts are not our thoughts. In a market where we bargain and calculate, He thinks in mercy. Where we see failure, He sees refining. This gap between His mind and ours is not a gulf to despair over—it is the space where hope lives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The heavens above the earth—how small we are beneath that measure. Yet He stoops to call us by name. His ways are higher not to mock our smallness, but to tell us we are held by a Love larger than all distance, older than all time.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rain and snow fall from the sky—no choice in it, no hesitation. They water, they feed, they grow things. His word works the same way: poured out freely, it waters the soul and brings forth fruit we may not see at first. The mechanics are certain as weather.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His word doesn't return empty. What He speaks does what He sends it to do. In a world of broken promises and wasted breath, this is solid ground. When He says something will be, our job is simply to trust and watch it take shape.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Joy and peace led out like a procession—mountains and hills singing, trees clapping. This is not quiet comfort but a visible feast of gladness. When the Lord restores, all of creation seems to wake and celebrate. Even the land knows His hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in this: where thorns choke and briers scratch, He plants cypress and myrtle—beauty from barrenness, usefulness from waste. The sign is eternal, carved into the land and into the heart. He remakes what sin has broken, still, forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
